Aston Villa's Champions League clash with Galatasaray plunged into chaos as Turkish police hunt for a fugitive LION spotted 10 miles from the stadium

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1572 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dailymail

⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Published: 12:24 EST, 23 November 2026 | Updated: 18:09 EST, 23 November 2026.
  • A lion has been spotted about ten miles from the stadium where Aston Villa are due to face Galatasaray in the Champions League on Tuesday.
  • In a bizarre development, Turkish security and wildlife personnel were on Monday searching for the animal​, believed to be roaming loose ‌in woodland north of Istanbul.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By TOM COLLOMOSSE, FOOTBALL REPORTER.

Published: 12:24 EST, 23 November 2026 | Updated: 18:09 EST, 23 November 2026.

A lion has been spotted about ten miles from the stadium where Aston Villa are due to face Galatasaray in the Champions League on Tuesday.

In a bizarre development, Turkish security and wildlife personnel were on Monday searching for the animal​, believed to be roaming loose ‌in woodland north of Istanbul.

Around 70 people, including police and other emergency personnel, have been involved in the search, with seven drones deployed. The animal was first sighted in Istanbul's Sariyer district, which is also where Galatasaray's RAMS Park is located.

According to local reports, personnel at a police station in ​the Zekeriyakoy area, north of the ​European side of Istanbul, reported seeing 'an animal ⁠resembling a lion' on surveillance cameras at ​around 9pm local time on Sunday (6pm GMT).

Extensive security measures have been put in place around the forested area where the animal is believed to be located and nearby villas. Access to and from the area is being controlled, while residents have been warned to remain cautious.

'The area where the lion is located has been identified, and every effort is being made to capture it alive,' the Istanbul Governor's Office remarked in a statement.

A lion has been spotted 10 miles from where Aston Villa are set to play in the Champions League on Tuesday.

The Istanbul Governor's Office said 'every effort' is being made to capture the lion alive.

Reaction to the lion's escape bordered on the surreal, with one outlet interviewing a person in a lion suit, wearing a Galatasaray shirt, about it. Galatasaray are nicknamed the Lions while Villa have a lion on their badge.

Gala defender Abdulkerim Bardakci was even asked about the matter, and replied: 'I want to say something because the whole country is talking about this right now. There's only one lion I keep at home, and that's my son.'.

Daily Mail Sport has contacted UEFA for an update.

There were even suggestions in Turkey that Villa had cancelled their training session at RAMS Park because of the lion, but Villa did their preparation at Bodymoor Heath for a very different reason – the state of the RAMS Park pitch.

European football chiefs are confident the playing surface will pose no risk to Aston Villa after conducting thorough inspections.

The Turkish giants have commissioned intensive work on the pitch and moved their most recent league game, against Samsunspor, to the stadium of rivals Istanbul Basaksehir.

It has been revealed that yet it is thought conditions will be some way from perfect and though Villa boss Unai Emery played it down, he will be anxious about injuries. 'We have to think that if there was a risk of injury, we wouldn't be playing on it,' he said. 'The pitch will be better or worse, for both teams.'.

Villa defender Ian Maatsen noted: 'We don't know anything about the pitch. They say it's in a little bit of a bad condition but that's no excuse. We have to see how the pitch is. We are ready.'.

Galatasaray coach Okan Buruk added: 'It was dug up again, another hybrid treatment was applied, and seeds were planted. There is also sand mixed into the pitch to help.'.

Villa, who have been followed abroad by Prince William this season, will take on Galatasaray.

Aston Villa shocked Europe by marching straight into the last 16 in the Champions League two seasons ago but a win over Galatasaray will put them on course to repeat it.

Unai Emery’s side have nine points from a possible 12 in the league phase and victory in Istanbul will give them one foot in the knockout rounds.

Daily Mail Sport looks at what Villa can expect from one of the toughest tests on the European calendar.

European football chiefs are confident Galatasaray’s pitch will pose no risk to Aston Villa after conducting thorough inspections of the playing surface at RAMS Park.

The Turkish giants have commissioned intensive work on the pitch and moved their most recent league game, against Samsunspor, to the stadium of rivals Istanbul Basaksehir.

Yet it is thought conditions will be some way from perfect and though Villa boss Unai Emery played it down, he will be anxious about injuries.

Villa defender Ian Maatsen noted: ‘We don't know anything about the pitch. They say it's in a little bit of a bad condition but that's no excuse. We have to see how the pitch is. We are ready.’.

Galatasaray coach Okan Buruk added: ‘It was dug up again, another hybrid treatment was applied, and seeds were planted. There is also sand mixed into the pitch to help.’.

Sources indicate that villa are back in their happy place. This city hosted their 3-0 win over Freiburg in the Europa League Final last May, though that game happened at Tupras Stadium, home of Besiktas.

Repeat that result here and Villa will be eyeing a top-eight finish – which they also achieved two years ago. That would allow them to skip the play-off round early next year and head straight into the last 16.

European football chiefs are confident Galatasaray’s pitch will pose no risk to Aston Villa (Source: X/Forza Cimbom).

Will Garnacho’s chance ever come?

Five months into his loan spell from Chelsea, Alejandro Garnacho is still waiting for his first competitive start for Aston Villa.

It has been revealed that when the Argentine moved to Villa Park, it was suggested that turning the temporary move into a £43million permanent deal would be a relative formality. Right now, that feels nearly impossible. Garnacho has featured for only 95 minutes this term and if Emery really did want the 22-year-old last summer, he has a funny way of showing it.

Indeed, Daily Mail Sport understands that even during Garnacho’s early days at the club, some Villa players were starting to wonder whether he would ever play regularly for Emery.

What next? There is believed to be no recall clause in the loan deal with Chelsea yet as Garnacho has only represented Villa this term, the clubs could agree to cancel the arrangement in January.

Born in Madrid, Garnacho was part of the youth system at Atletico before joining Manchester United. With four Argentines in the Atletico squad, plus another in boss Diego Simeone, that might be worth keeping an eye on.

Sources indicate that yet it is thought that neither Galatasaray nor Fenerbahce, who were monitoring Garnacho last summer, are in the market for a high-wage signing in January. That would close off one potential escape route.

Thanks to the sales of Morgan Rogers, Ezri Konsa and Youri Tielemans that brought in nearly £200million, Villa were able to spend heavily in the summer.

According to recent reports, to invest again in the winter, they will probably need to attract offers for some fringe players. As well as Garnacho, Tammy Abraham and Lamare Bogarde have been overlooked by Emery recently. Abraham has fallen behind Brian Madjo in the pecking order, though the 17-year-old was not included in the Champions League squad, while Bogarde’s only starts have been in the Carabao Cup, which is always low on Emery’s priority list. Selling Bogarde would also deliver pure profit – crucial for a club forever fighting to stay in line with Premier League and UEFA spending rules.

There were always going to be bumps in the road this season for Villa, and there will likely be more. In last Saturday’s dispiriting 0-0 draw with Sunderland, there were only two players – Emi Buendia and Pau Torres – in the starting XI who were also in the line-up for the Europa League Final. Replacing the six who departed will take time.

In their commendable attempts to bring down the average age of the squad, Villa find themselves with a surplus of attackers but no midfield controller since the departure of Tielemans, and they also look vulnerable in central defence.

Tyrone Mings turns 34 in March and Victor Lindelof was 32 in July while Taylor Harwood-Bellis must find his feet rapidly in one of the most demanding competitions in the world. It is tough without Konsa.

According to recent reports, elsewhere, there are possibly too many options. George Hemmings and then Alysson have forced their way into the side at different times this season, meaning fewer opportunities for Ibrahim Mbaye, who cost nearly £50million from Paris Saint-Germain last summer. Johan Manzambi has played regularly and with John McGinn and Buendia also in the mix, a player like Garnacho has a near-impossible task to convince Emery.

Alejandro Garnacho is still waiting for his first competitive start for Aston Villa - five months after joining from Chelsea.

Scouts from across Europe have been watching Galatasaray’s matches this season and Aleksey Batrakov is usually the reason why.

The 21-year-old Russian playmaker has six goals – including four in the Champions League – and four assists since his £21million move from Lokomotiv Moscow and is one of the breakout stars of the world game.

He caught the eye of Paris Saint-Germain while playing for Lokomotiv and Barcelona boss Hansi Flick has praised him.

The last Russian to play in the Premier League was Pavel Pogrebnyak, whose last game for Reading was against West Ham in May 2013.

Given the current geopolitical situation, Pogrebnyak will surely hold that record for some time to come.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Matt Law | 24 Nov 2026 11:51, Last updated: 24 Nov 2026 11:52.

Barcelona will continue their Champions League league stage campaign with a contest against Azerbaijani outfit Sabah on Wednesday evening.

The La Liga giants are fifth in the overall table on nine points, while Sabah are 31st, collecting three points from their opening four matches of the 2026-27 league stage.

Here, Sports Mole provides details of how to tune into the contest.

The Champions League match will kick off at 5.45pm UK time on Wednesday.

The Champions League match between Sabah and Barcelona will be played at Baku Olympic Stadium.

Boasting a seating capacity of just under 70,000, it is the largest stadium in Azerbaijan.

The Champions League match will be shown live on TNT Sports 4.

TNT Sports is also available as an add-on for Amazon's Prime Video app.

Goals will be posted on the FootballOnTNT X account, while highlights will also be uploaded to the TNT Sports Football YouTube channel after the match.

History will be made on Wednesday, as Sabah and Barcelona prepare to lock horns for the first time, and the hosts will be eyeing a stunning win over the La Liga champions.

Sabah have won one and lost three of their matches in the league stage of the competition, while Barcelona have a record of three wins and one defeat.

The Owls had never played in the European Cup before this season, and they will now be taking on one of the biggest club teams in European football.

Barcelona lost in the last-16 stage of last season's Champions League to Atletico Madrid, so there is clear room for improvement during the current campaign.

Sabah are the huge underdogs entering this match, but the fact that Lamine Yamal will not be involved for Barcelona due to an injury will hand the hosts a degree of confidence.

Carrick’s United are in crisis and now spotlight is on Wilcox

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that michael Carrick had urged his Manchester United players to come out and fight. But nobody could have imagined quite how Lisandro Martínez would interpret that message.

By the end of an extraordinary evening in Madrid, where United went 1-0 down inside a minute and never recovered against Atlético Madrid, Martínez had blown the lid off any pretence of all being well at the club as he launched a lacerating assault on the club’s executives.

United had come into this getting battered from all sides and when Pablo Barrios put Atlético ahead, Jamie Carragher’s pre-match assessment about how things could get “very messy, very quickly” for all involved at Old Trafford must have been ringing in the ears of the travelling supporters.

ATLETICO ARE AHEAD IN JUST 53 SECONDS! ⚡️ A nightmare start for United at the Metropolitano Stadium 😬 https://t.co/TdOwoXxopn.

It has been revealed that they certainly know how to make life difficult for themselves. Leny Yoro’s 74th-minute red card pretty much ended hopes of them taking something from the game.

In a recent development, ademola Lookman scored Atlético’s second soon after and Carrick was staring at another defeat. And so they now move on to a big game at Leeds on Sunday. This was not the result Carrick would have wanted – and that is before what happened off the pitch.

Ademola Lookman PUNISHES a 10-man Man United 💥 https://t.co/GHKYIHGhNC.

Another defeat intensified the pressure on Carrick but Martínez left nobody under any illusions that he felt the finger should be pointed not simply at another manager or the players, but the hierarchy above him.

It was extraordinary to see a player speaking out so publicly in this fashion against his own bosses.

But Martínez pulled no punches, even going as far as singling out Jason Wilcox, the director of football, as he criticised the club’s summer transfer business and effectively accused the club of failing Carrick and the players in the window.

To what extent Martínez’s comments mirror the views of the wider dressing room is unclear, but you have to wonder where Carrick and United go from here.

On the one hand, Martínez was providing a show of support for his manager by attacking the people above him. At the same time, he has presented Carrick with a disciplinary problem to address.

Lisandro Martínez did NOT hold back after United's loss to Atletico 😬👀 https://t.co/OGo25Pzd30.

And United have enough troubles as it is without a senior member of Carrick’s dressing room turning so squarely against the club’s power brokers.

According to recent reports, martínez was probably only giving voice to what many fans have been saying since an underwhelming transfer window closed with more questions than answers. But for a player to talk in such blunt, excoriating terms resonated more loudly than anything a supporter or United’s most caustic critic could say.

The message was simple: you can sack all the managers you want but until you pull together a squad worthy of United’s name and give the man at the helm the tools to compete, the club will struggle to escape this cycle of mediocrity.

In a recent development, no one can reasonably argue United’s window was a success. They went into it with the hopes of landing Elliot Anderson and other premium midfielders but ended up going for numbers over proven quality or pedigree. Youri Tielemans, Andrey Santos and Carlos Baleba were not a trio of signings anyone expected at the start of summer, not even the club itself.

There were glaring concerns to address in defence, not least at left-back, and at centre-forward but a quality alternative to Luke Shaw never materialised and no back-up was signed for Benjamin Sesko, who was missing for four months with a shin injury that has since resurfaced and which could keep him out for a while yet.

Having done so well to lead United to third and take them back into the Champions League, Carrick would have expected further backing than he got in the summer. Ever the tech giant man, he has been too polite to criticise that lack of investment. But the cat is out of the bag now Martínez has had his say.

It now places the spotlight on Wilcox. United head to Elland Road on Sunday and that was the scene of Rúben Amorim’s final meltdown as manager. Two days after he blew up in a meeting with Wilcox at United’s Carrington training base, Amorim took aim at the director of football and others at the club, demanding they “do their job” and repeatedly declaring that he had come to Old Trafford to “be the manager, not to be the coach”.

Sources indicate that good evening and welcome to live coverage of the Champions League tie between Atlético Madrid and Manchester United from the Metropolitano. The two sides had contrasting fortunes in their opening fixtures in this competition, Man Utd beating Azerbaijan’s Sabah 4-0 at Old Trafford a month ago while Atléti were defeated by Liverpool who came back from 1-0 down to win 2-1.

But domestically it is the other way round – Michael Carrick’s side have made the club’s worst start in the league for 40 years with one win, three draws and two defeats and have been knocked out of the League Cup. Those of us who watch them regularly – purely because of occupational obligations in this instance – have been surprised by how poor they have been. The results have been bad but the performances even worse.

They seem to lack players who can play on the front foot, who have the athletic dynamism required in this league and too many self-indulgent forward players who either can’t be bothered to help out their team-mates or cannot concentrate long enough to do so. Spooked by their lack of pace in defence and midfield, they are hidebound by caution, dropping ever deeper, ever more reliant on counter-attacking despite the blatant disconnect between the front four and back six. If they drift through this match and Sunday’s trip to Elland Road, Carrick may join the long list of Ineos-driven managerial mis-steps.

It has been revealed that atlético have won six of eight in La Liga and have been defeated only once. They are five points behind Barcelona in second and have score 18 goals and let in eight, which may seem a curious thing to include in a preview but it is done to emphasise that many fans’ perception of Diego Simeone’s team are out of date. Back in the days of Diego Godín, Gabi, Juanfran et all, six wins a draw and a defeat would have had goals for of about 10 and goals against of maybe three.

Simeone is a martinet about attitude not systems or styles and his team have evolved, with the World Cup-winner Alex Baena, who has scored four goals so far, driving them on. He has reintegrated Julián Alvarez, too, after his brazen attempt to force a move to Barcelona so incensed Atléti fans that it seemed they would drive him out of the club. Simeone refused to let Alvarez get his own way and he is now buckling down. Ten years ago Simeone would have bitten his head off.

In a recent development, the one surviving veteran in the squad from that first of El Cholo’s Liga winning sides and the two Champions League finals, victory in which would represent Simeone’s crowning achievement, is the midfielder Koke. Remarkably, if he features today, the 34-year-old midfielder will be making his 750th first-team appearance as an Atlético player.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • As the news spread from one mathematician to the next, panic set in.
  • Mathematicians astounded by AI and human-written proofs of iconic Riemann hypothesis.
  • Mathematicians astounded by AI and human-written proofs of iconic Riemann hypothesis.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

As the news spread from one mathematician to the next, panic set in. On 6 October, OpenAI, the maker of ChatGPT, released more than 700 preprints written by AI, claiming to have solved more than 300 major open problems in mathematics. Some researchers stayed up all night combing through the papers that the manufacturer had posted, anxious to know whether their entire research programmes had been rendered obsolete overnight.

Mathematicians astounded by AI and human-written proofs of iconic Riemann hypothesis.

Mathematicians astounded by AI and human-written proofs of iconic Riemann hypothesis.

According to recent reports, depending on who you ask, this was either the most progress or the most catastrophic development ever to happen in one day in the history of the field — or both. Either way, mathematicians realized that their profession would never be the same. “It’s probably the end of mathematics as we know it,” theoretical physicist Miranda Cheng stated at an emergency meeting on mathematics and AI at the Royal Society in London in late October. Many of the papers cracked problems by combining ideas from disparate parts of the discipline, leveraging a universality of knowledge that no human could ever match — and leaving even some of the world’s smartest people feeling completely outdone.

It has been revealed that since then, one of the field’s greatest outstanding challenges, the Riemann hypothesis, also appears to have been solved with AI assistance. And mathematicians across the world have joined frantic collective efforts to confront challenges raised by AI’s advances, from how to evaluate and publish research papers to how to raise future generations of mathematicians. Some see the risk as existential. If mathematical problem-solving becomes mainly a machine endeavour — seen as a utility like water or electricity — then their profession could lose its status in society and human expertise might start to dwindle.

“It’s a challenge like we’ve never faced in mathematics — or in academia as a whole,” says Simon Machado, a mathematician at the Swiss Federal Institute of Technology (ETH) in Zurich.

In a recent development, the bombshell paper drop in October came on the heels of earlier shocks to the field. OpenAI, which is based in San Francisco, California, released a batch of ten important results in August and, in early September, followed up with a historic solution to the Navier–Stokes problem about how fluids flow. The firm had been making noises to indicate that much more was to come. Still, many researchers were surprised by the enormity of the 6 October release. “To just see it as a giant list, without the care and thought and the love that goes into doing this work on a normal basis, it was really jarring,” says Catherine Cossaboom, a master’s student in mathematics at the University of Oxford, UK.

OpenAI posts 700 maths preprints online: mathematicians are up in arms.

OpenAI posts 700 maths preprints online: mathematicians are up in arms.

Perhaps no source has documented the moment better than Proofs and Prompts, an online forum that publishes essays on the impact of AI on mathematics. An 8 October post titled “100+ reactions to 100+ solutions” collected immediate reactions from dozens of students and career researchers to OpenAI’s 6 October drop. Some wrote poems, others quoted the writers Leo Tolstoy and Stanisław Lem, still others posted fragments from the Gospels (in the original Greek). One contribution reinterpreted the lyrics of ‘Jolene’ by the late country singer Dolly Parton:.

And I can easily understand / How you could easily take my math / But you don’t know what it means to me, AI.

Recent findings suggest that the tone ranged from the enthusiastic to the angry and the despondent. “Some of them made me really feel heartbroken,” claims Albane Théry, an applied mathematician at the University of Warwick in Coventry, UK, who is one of the volunteer moderators of the forum.

Few subfields of mathematics were spared and some were thoroughly ravaged. “Not a single one of the major open problems I have publicly mentioned throughout my career was left untouched,” Fields Medal winner Hugo Duminil-Copin wrote to Proofs and Prompts. “I expected that one day we would be surpassed, and that it would happen systematically. But yesterday’s announcement hit with a force I had not anticipated.”.

Hugo Duminil-Copin fears that AI will eclipse human understanding of mathematics.Credit: Chris Peus.

Duminil-Copin, who is at the University of Geneva in Switzerland, specializes in the theory of transitions in complex systems — such as those that determine how information or infection filters through social networks or how metals can acquire magnetization. (OpenAI’s rival Anthropic, also in San Francisco, had already claimed to have solved a major result in this field in late August.).

It has been revealed that another field that bore a massive impact was the theory of groups — some of the most ubiquitous structures across mathematics, physics and other disciplines. For example, the possible ways of shuffling a deck of cards — and what happens when you revert a shuffle or combine several together — constitute a group, as do the infinite possible ways of rotating a solid object in 3D.

OpenAI’s August batch already contained the solution to a key problem on groups. Soon after its release, during a YouTube interview, Francesco Fournier-Facio, a group theorist at Heriot-Watt University in Edinburgh, UK, mentioned two other problems that mathematicians could now attack with the help of AI. Within days, he was emailed by a PhD student in computational biology who had used OpenAI’s large language model (LLM) GPT 5.6 Sol to solve one of those problems.

Can maths survive AI? Fields medallist Terence Tao calls for a ‘Maths 2.0’ world.

Can maths survive AI? Fields medallist Terence Tao calls for a ‘Maths 2.0’ world.

According to recent reports, fournier-Facio says that OpenAI’s October dump was even more impactful for him personally. It included the solution to a problem on which he had been actively working, called the Boone–Higman conjecture. Overall, OpenAI released solutions to perhaps eight of the top ten problems that Fournier-Facio had dreamed of solving during his career, he told Nature.

Industry observers note that but the most stunning AI result relates to what many researchers see as the most important open problem in all of mathematics. The Riemann hypothesis, a question that was posed in the mid-nineteenth century by the German mathematician Bernhard Riemann, centres on whether prime numbers are scattered across the set of all whole numbers in a way that is essentially as unpredictable as it could be.

In a recent development, AI assistance seems to have cracked it. First, OpenAI proved a partial result, called the quasi-Riemann hypothesis, in its October dump. Then, on 20 November, Anthropic mathematician Levent Alpöge announced that he had found a proof of the full Riemann hypothesis, working with Claude, the firm’s AI assistant. However, that was promptly followed by a non-AI assisted proof by Rome-based mathematician Alessandro Masullo, which he had been working on for years. “If this fully checks out, it is clearly a historic milestone in mathematics,” says number theorist James Maynard, a Fields Medal winner at the University of Oxford.

According to recent reports, maynard and many other researchers are excited by AI technology. It is “quite likely to unleash a golden age of mathematical discovery”, he said at the meeting. Another mathematician, Antoine Tilloy at the Mines Paris engineering school, part of PSL University, uses the metaphor that doing mathematics with AI is like riding a dragon: the researcher is still in charge, but the dragon gives them supernatural powers.

‘Mathematics is more than a mechanical process’ — why I think the field will survive OpenAI’s disruption.

‘Mathematics is more than a mechanical process’ — why I think the field will survive OpenAI’s disruption.

But the speed at which AI proofs are emerging has already produced an immediate negative reaction. For one, mathematicians, who have long prided themselves on their field’s culture of openness, are now wary of discussing their work in public. “People are even scared to put out an abstract for a talk they are about to give on ongoing work,” says Jakub Dobrowolski, a PhD candidate at Queen Mary University of London. “Nobody wants to share new ideas because of the speed at which somebody else can take them and write a paper,” says Peter Sarnak, a number theorist at Princeton University in New Jersey.

Industry observers note that and although established researchers say that they are both thrilled and anxious about reinventing their discipline with AI, younger generations are much more fearful. As Maynard and other established mathematicians acknowledge, the technology already poses severe problems in relation to how to assess merit when peer-reviewing mathematics work that might have been done mostly with AI, and how to train and educate the next generation of mathematicians.

Industry observers note that “How do we train people if a good PhD thesis can be prompted out of an LLM? The response from people who are in permanent positions tends to be ‘We’re going to see and discuss’,” indicates Théry. “But the timescale for that could be too long for postdoc or PhD candidates who will be out of a job in nine months.”.

Many early-career researchers told Nature that this uncertainty is their main source of anxiety right now. “While it is clear that faculty are working hard to find long-term solutions to the problems we are all facing, there doesn’t seem to be as much guidance on what to do in the meantime,” claims Jad Hamdan, a postdoc mathematician at the University of Oxford. AI poses “more danger the younger you are, and the less experienced you are”, adds Dobrowolski. The toughest problem could be working out how to write a proposal for a research programme that might span two or three years, or more, Dobrowolski says. “Is it realistic? Now I feel like whatever I propose might just expire within a year.”.

Mathematicians are developing rules for AI use — other fields should follow.

Mathematicians are developing rules for AI use — other fields should follow.

Recent findings suggest that A UK survey of graduate students and academic mathematicians last month by the Martingale Foundation in London found that PhD students in particular are much less optimistic about AI’s impact than are established researchers. Asked if AI would “weaken their development as mathematicians”, 89% of students agreed, compared with only 68% of academics.

Starting with La Gazzetta dello Sport, they gave the team’s overall performance a score of 8 out of 10, which is the same mark that they gave Amorim for his selections and tactical handling of what could have been a tough game on paper.

Rabiot was the Serie A Man of the Match and he gets the crown from La Gazzetta too, scoring an 8. The worst performer was Davide Bartesaghi, who struggled in his battle with Ghedjemis and got a 5.5.

Sources indicate that moreira matched Rabiot with an 8, while Pulisic and Luka Modric were given a 7.5. Four players scored a 7: Yunus Musah, Ramos, Jashari and Cisse. Sankhoun Diawara (6.5) passed the test, with Koni De Winter, Strahinja Pavlovic and Pervis Estupinan being given a 6.

According to recent reports, corriere dello Sport were a tad harsher with their scoring, giving Rabiot a 7.5 as the highest score. Jashari, Moreira, Modric, Pulisic and Ramos were handed a 7. They gave Cisse a 6.5, and everyone else got a passing score. Amorim (7.5) was also praised.

Tuttosport meanwhile gave Rabiot an 8, distributing 7.5s instead to Moreira, Modric, Pulisic and the coach Amorim. Scores of 7 went to Jashari, Musah, Ramos and Cisse. Gila, De Winter and Diawara got given a 6.5, and everyone else a 6.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Oliver Thomas | 24 Nov 2026 12:22.

Liverpool are reportedly among a number of clubs interested in signing Borussia Monchengladbach wonderkid Wael Mohya.

Earlier this month, the 17-year-old attacker earned his first-ever senior international call-up to Jurgen Klopp’s Germany squad after making a notable impression as a first-team regular at club level.

Mohya broke into Monchengladbach’s senior side midway through last season and became the club’s youngest-ever goalscorer against Bayern Munich in March of this year.

He has since developed into an increasingly influential player under head coach Alexander Blessin this term, featuring in all 10 Bundesliga matches as well as two DFB-Pokal games.

Mohya became the fourth youngest-player in Bundesliga history to score in consecutive games in October, contributing with a goal and an assist in a standout display in a 3-2 win against Stuttgart.

The dynamic and versatile attacker, who is comfortable operating centrally or out wide, has produced several impressive performances that have subsequently caught the eye of some of Europe’s biggest clubs.

According to TEAMtalk, Andoni Iraola’s Liverpool have shown concrete interest in Mohya and have intensively scouted the teenager.

The report adds the Reds are ‘ready to battle’ with high-flying Brighton & Hove Albion, who at the moment sit second in the Premier League table and have also been closely monitoring the attacker.

Bundesliga giants Bayern Munich, Borussia Dortmund, Bayer Leverkusen and RB Leipzig are also stated to be keeping an eye on Mohya’s progress, while Real Madrid, Barcelona and AC Milan are some of the big clubs abroad who have recently entered the race for his signature.

As things stand, Monchengladbach are yet to receive any formal offers for Mohya or enter negotiations with another club despite growing interest in his services.

Mohya’s contract is due to expire in June 2028, and Monchengladbach sporting director Rouven Schroder recently insisted that “he is definitely not for sale in January,” adding: “The rest will depend on how the market develops.”.

The youngster is viewed as a key part of Monchengladbach’s plans for this season, and it is understood that an offer in the region of €45m (£37.7m) is what it would take to persuade the German club to open talks over a possible sale in the coming transfer windows.

Gary Neville slaps himself in the FACE in bizarre on-air moment after Man United's humiliation at Anfield - weeks after claiming his old club are 'in a better place' than Liverpool

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Published: 04:43 EST, 23 November 2026 | Updated: 10:28 EST, 24 November 2026.
  • Gary Neville showcased the dramatic decline of Manchester United this season as he bizarrely slapped himself in the face on Sky Sports after his former side's 4-0, 10-man, defeat to Liverpool at Anfield.
  • Neville's dramatic example of Man United's lack of hunger and sharpness came in stark contrast to his pre-season proclamations for the side, when he informed his co-pundit Jamie Carragher that he believed that then-manager Michael Carrick's starting XI was stronger than Liverpool's after a summer recruitment drive.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By TAMARA PRENN, SENIOR SPORTS REPORTER.

Published: 04:43 EST, 23 November 2026 | Updated: 10:28 EST, 24 November 2026.

Gary Neville showcased the dramatic decline of Manchester United this season as he bizarrely slapped himself in the face on Sky Sports after his former side's 4-0, 10-man, defeat to Liverpool at Anfield.

Neville's dramatic example of Man United's lack of hunger and sharpness came in stark contrast to his pre-season proclamations for the side, when he informed his co-pundit Jamie Carragher that he believed that then-manager Michael Carrick's starting XI was stronger than Liverpool's after a summer recruitment drive.

Instead, Man United saw their numbers reduced inside the opening stages of the game after a reckless challenge by Leny Yoro, and 2-0 down after 13 minutes, with the club legend resorting to drastic methods to convey the side's weaknesses.

Of his old club's defenders, he mentioned: 'I never see any of them on their toes, alert, looking like they've got something fixed in here', before pointing to his head.

In a recent development, 'I never see any of them look like that,' he added. 'They look like that -'.

Neville then stared into the middle distance for a few moments to share the blankness he sees on the faces of the back line, before spitting: 'Wake up!'.

Gary Neville took to slapping himself to convey the lack of focus he sees in Man United's stars.

The club legend had previously tipped his old side to have a stronger XI than Liverpool's.

But when the two teams met at Anfield, Man United were left woefully exposed after going down to 10 men.

The Overlap broadcaster then slapped his own face a number of times repeating 'wake up!' before adding: 'You play for Man United'.

The gesture left Carragher in stitches, with the Anfield icon collapsing onto the sofa in hysterics - although less impressed with Roy Keane, who displayed his usual sangfroid.

So tickled by the moment was the former Liverpool star that he later changed his profile picture on social media site X to a still image of Neville's hand catching his face.

Neville had more sharp criticism for Man United's defensive selection assessing the inclusion of Matthijs de Ligt in the starting line-up.

The Dutch defender has been out of Premier League action for 51 weeks after suffering a back injury, but was named by Mauricio Pochettino in his first-ever XI.

According to recent reports, 'I have a lot of sympathy for him,' Neville admitted. 'It's like playing football after having six pints. It's a strange feeling.

'I have a lot of sympathy for him, it's alarming to watch.'.

Less sympathy for Man United's players came from Keane, who attacked the team - and Neville and Carragher - after the heavy defeat at Anfield confirmed the club's worst start in over 53 years.

The firebrand midfielder was on his usual caustic form as he assessed the damage, hitting out at those who might have accepted the score line, having feared a greater deficit.

Recent findings suggest that 'If I hear that one more time from the lads in the commentary that 4-0 is not too bad when you're down to 10 men - has a team ever got a result with 10 men before?' Keane said immediately after the final whistle. 'It can be done.

'I thought United were desperate. I thought they were so bad and everyone and Nev, who played for Man United saying 4-0 ain't bad.'.

'(The red card) doesn't help but you're telling me they couldn't have done better? They lost 4-0 with 10 men, that's not too bad? Has a team ever got a result with 10 men? It can be done. At least show a bit more fight, a bit more quality - I can't believe what I'm hearing from people.

Recent findings suggest that 'You played for the club, saying 4-0 isn't too bad. Wow. Fans are applauding. Applauding what? Performing rubbish. Liverpool were excellent, but how easy did United make it for them? I can't believe what I'm watching sometimes.

In a recent development, 'This team two years ago finished 15th. The last year or two, we're talking. We're blaming the board, blaming ownership, blaming managers.

'When do the players take responsibility for some decision-making? Liverpool probably should have scored eight, probably eight or nine, unbelievable chances they had. And everyone's coming off the pitch saying 4 is not too bad? I feel like swearing.'.

The difference between the two teams felt a far cry from Neville's late-summer prediction, when he told Carragher that he had greater hopes for Carrick and Man United over incoming manager Andoni Iraola at Liverpool.

'I think Manchester United are currently in a better place than Liverpool,' Neville mentioned in August. 'Would you agree?'.

Carragher stated that he did not, and will have been confident in his assessment on Sunday night.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Ellis Stevens | 24 Nov 2026 12:23.
  • Torreense welcome Celtic to Estadio Municipal de Leiria on Thursday night for a matchday five clash in the league phase of the Europa League.
  • The hosts are 19th in the standings with six points from four games, while the visitors are 32nd with three points after four matches.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Ellis Stevens | 24 Nov 2026 12:23.

Torreense welcome Celtic to Estadio Municipal de Leiria on Thursday night for a matchday five clash in the league phase of the Europa League.

The hosts are 19th in the standings with six points from four games, while the visitors are 32nd with three points after four matches.

Torreense made history by defeating Sporting Lisbon 2-1 in the Taca de Portugal final last season, marking the club's first major trophy and securing their qualification to the Europa League.

Torreense, as a result, became the first non-top flight club to qualify for the revamped league phase of the competition, and Azul-grenas have performed admirably in their opening four fixtures.

Thursday's hosts have secured two wins and suffered two defeats in their first four games, leaving Torreense placed 19th in the league phase table and on course to qualify for the knockouts.

The latest of those victories, a dramatic 3-2 win against Ararat-Armenia that featured two goals in stoppage time to come from 2-1 down to secure the win, came under new boss Joao Nuno, who was appointed after Luis Miguel Valado Tralhao mutually agreed to step down as manager.

Nuno recorded one win and one draw in his first two games, but the manager has since suffered back-to-back defeats heading into this match, leaving Torreense eager to avoid enduring a third consecutive loss.

Torreense will draw confidence from their impressive displays in the Europa League, while visitors Celtic have shown signs of weakness in this competition this term.

The Bhoys have won only one of their four league phase fixtures, alongside three defeats, scoring just six goals and conceding a considerable 11 goals in that time.

Martin O'Neill's side actually lost each of their first three league phase fixtures, results that coincided with a miserable run across all competitions, during which they recorded six defeats, one draw and just three wins between mid-September and the beginning of November.

However, a 3-2 triumph over Besiktas on matchday four of the league phase, featuring an 87th-minute winner from Camilo Duran, has sparked a three-game winning run, subsequently defeating both Kilmarnock (1-0) and St Mirren (4-1).

Celtic will be looking to extend that winning streak and secure just their second win of the league phase on Thursday, with the Bhoys hoping to move closer to the qualification places.

While Celtic have returned to winning ways in recent matches, concerns remain about their form on the road, having lost three of their last five away fixtures across all competitions.

Torreense form (all competitions):.

Celtic form (all competitions):.

Torreense will be without Jorge Aguirre for Thursday's fixture after the forward was sent off in the matchday four clash with Ararat-Armenia, and Adama Baradji is also not expected to feature due to an injury concern.

In Aguirre's absence, Musa Drammeh, who scored in the defeat to Benfica last time out, should lead the line, with Carlos Reina providing support in attacking midfield.

Meanwhile, Duran, who has scored 14 goals in 22 appearances for Celtic this season, should lead the line, with Sebastian Tounekti, Benjamin Nygren and Haissem Hassan providing attacking support.

Further back, Alex Oxlade-Chamberlain and Callum McGregor could feature at the base of midfield, with Cameron Carter-Vickers and Liam Scales in central defence.

Torreense possible starting lineup:.

Olmeta; Mutombo, Diadie, Volnei, Vazquez; Marques, Alfaro; Guerrero, Reina, Jean; Drammeh.

Celtic possible starting lineup:.

Johnstone; Lotomba, Carter-Vickers, Scales, Tierney; McGregor, Oxlade-Chamberlain; Hassan, Nygren, Tounekti; Duran.

Although Celtic have struggled on the road in recent matches and shown signs of weakness in the Europa League, the away side should have the quality to overcome their second-division hosts and secure the win.

Chelsea news: £75m player seriously considered retirement under Enzo Maresca

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (546 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Oliver Thomas | 24 Nov 2026 12:42.
  • Chelsea defender Wesley Fofana has admitted that he seriously considered retiring from football during Enzo Maresca’s time in charge at Stamford Bridge.
  • The one-cap France international joined the West Londoners from Leicester City for a reported £75m in the summer of 2022 and has since played 81 times for the club across all competitions.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Oliver Thomas | 24 Nov 2026 12:42.

Chelsea defender Wesley Fofana has admitted that he seriously considered retiring from football during Enzo Maresca’s time in charge at Stamford Bridge.

The one-cap France international joined the West Londoners from Leicester City for a reported £75m in the summer of 2022 and has since played 81 times for the club across all competitions.

Fofana’s career at Chelsea has largely been disrupted by injury, missing a total of 41 matches during Maresca’s 18-month reign with the Blues.

While Fofana began the 2024-25 season fit after recovering from a year-long ACL tear, two major hamstring injuries wiped out nearly six months of his campaign.

The 25-year-old centre-back has since opened up about how the psychological strain that came with a rash of injuries almost led to the decision to prematurely call time on his career.

Speaking in an interview for Zack Nani TV, as quoted by the Evening Standard, Fofana mentioned: “There was a period when I was recovering from my cruciate ligament and meniscus injuries.

“Then I suffered two consecutive hamstring strains under Enzo Maresca, when I really decided: ‘That’s it, I’m retiring, I’m done playing.’ I was serious.

Recent findings suggest that “I really wanted to stop, because, for the first time in my life, I wasn’t happy anymore. It wasn’t just about being injured or not playing; my whole life was completely shattered. I wasn’t myself anymore. I sincerely believed that, in the future, I would only get injured.

“I thought to myself: ‘That’s it, football isn’t for me, I’m too fragile.’ I even used Abou Diaby as an example. I thought to myself: ’I guess I’m the Abou Diaby of our generation. There has to be someone like that, and it happened to me. It’s my destiny, I accept it.’”.

Industry observers note that fofana added: “Of course, I was very sad and didn’t want to stop, because I was living my dream. At that point, I called my agents so we could sit down and talk, telling them, ‘Okay, I’ve decided to retire.’.

“They started analysing the situation with me, talking about contracts and all that: ‘It’s simple, you still have several years left on your contract, and there’s a lot of money to be made.

“Even if you really decide to stop playing, you still have to come every day, keep smiling, and even if you’re injured, you have to honour your contract for your future.’.

According to recent reports, “But at that moment, I really felt that the pain football caused me far outweighed the joy, so why continue? I was in pain almost 100 per cent of the time.

“Every time I gritted my teeth, played a few games, and just started to find a little love and joy in life again, bang, I’d get injured again.”.

Fofana has since made positive progress in building up his strength and fitness; he played 38 times for Chelsea in all competitions last season and has started seven of the first 11 Premier League matches under new manager Xabi Alonso so far this term.

Last month, Alonso publicly backed Fofana as an "notable," "focused," and "mature" first-team figure, who is under contract at Stamford Bridge until the summer of 2029.

Tottenham handed new James Maddison concern before Sunderland as training video emerges

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (441 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Ben Knapton | 24 Nov 2026 12:48.
  • Tottenham Hotspur have been handed a potential latest concern over James Maddison's fitness ahead of Sunday's Premier League clash with Sunderland.
  • The Lilywhites hit the road to face the Black Cats at the Stadium of Light this Sunday, aiming to register their fifth win from their last six Premier League matches.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Ben Knapton | 24 Nov 2026 12:48.

Tottenham Hotspur have been handed a potential latest concern over James Maddison's fitness ahead of Sunday's Premier League clash with Sunderland.

The Lilywhites hit the road to face the Black Cats at the Stadium of Light this Sunday, aiming to register their fifth win from their last six Premier League matches.

Spurs' recent resurgence has propelled them into the top half of the Premier League table, as they bounced back from their 1-0 defeat at Leeds United by dispatching Ipswich Town 2-0 on home soil.

Roberto De Zerbi's men got the better of the Tractor Boys despite the absence of Sandro Tonali, who was a last-minute omission from the matchday squad due to illness.

The Italian was filmed being put through his paces with the team in Tuesday's open training session, though, handing Spurs a welcome boost ahead of their trek north.

However, according to Sky Sports News journalist Michael Bridge, Maddison was restricted to indoor work, raising fears of another potential fitness concern for the playmaker.

Sources indicate that sandro Tonali back after missing the win over Ipswich. James Maddison doing indoor work. #THFC https://t.co/EsvY9oqNqb.

Maddison has only made three Premier League starts this season, having spent the majority of the 2025-26 campaign recovering from a serious ACL issue before also picking up a shoulder problem.

The 30-year-old was an unused substitute against Crystal Palace and Leeds earlier this month, and he was taken off in the 64th minute of Saturday's victory over Ipswich.

It is not clear whether Maddison's absence from team training was down to a genuine latest injury for the Englishman, or if he is simply being protected ahead of the weekend's fixture.

Nevertheless, for a player who has already missed 73 games for club and country since joining Tottenham from Leicester City in 2023, any minor fitness development could set off alarm bells in Spurs fans' heads.

While Maddison's situation will be closely monitored, Tonali's return from illness is one of two early boosts that Tottenham have received for the trip to Sunderland.

The Black Cats will be unable to call on Kevin Danso this weekend, as the on-loan Tottenham defender is ineligible to face his parent club.

Danso's absence may not have a massive bearing on Regis Le Bris's selection, though, as the Austrian has been an unused substitute in each of Sunderland's last three Premier League games.

Danso started each of the Black Cats' first five top-flight matches of the latest season, but he has not played a minute of Premier League football since being sent off against Bournemouth on October 18.

#118138. Rabiot and Ruben’s rampant Rossoneri: All the key stats from AC Milan 5-1 Frosinone

Rabiot and Ruben’s rampant Rossoneri: All the key stats from AC Milan 5-1 Frosinone

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (461 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Sempremilan

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • AC Milan produced their best attacking display of the season on Sunday night as they put five goals past Frosinone at San Siro.
  • Industry observers note that an own-goal from Gabriele Calvani early on set the tone, with Goncalo Ramos, Ardon Jashari, Alphadjo Cisse and Christian Pulisic all netting in the rout.
  • It has been revealed that read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

AC Milan produced their best attacking display of the season on Sunday night as they put five goals past Frosinone at San Siro.

Industry observers note that an own-goal from Gabriele Calvani early on set the tone, with Goncalo Ramos, Ardon Jashari, Alphadjo Cisse and Christian Pulisic all netting in the rout. The ruthless counter-attacking display moves Milan back inside the top four, after wins from Como, Roma and Lazio earlier in the round.

It has been revealed that read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

It has been revealed that the match stats make for interesting reading. Milan edged possession with 54%, generating 2.50 Expected Goals – so scoring double what they created – but also having five substantial chances which matches the number of goals scored.

According to recent reports, frosinone remarkably had more shots in total (15 to 12), but they were more wasteful with only three on target to the Rossoneri’s eight. The visitors also racked up nine corners, the most Milan have conceded all season.

📊 The stats from the win against Frosinone. pic.twitter.com/ERVTj98m9Y.

— MilanData📊 (@acmilandata) November 22, 2026.

Only Nereo Rocco’s (29) and Lajos Czeizler’s (31) Milan sides scored more goals than Ruben Amorim’s (28) in their first 12 matches in charge in Serie A.

Adrien Rabiot is the first Milan midfielder to be involved in at least one goal (including goals and assists) in seven consecutive Serie A appearances since Kaká in 2004, and he became the first midfielder in the last 20 years of Serie A with more than 10 goals in his first 10 games in a single season.

With his sixth goal in his 10th Serie A appearance for Milan at 20 years and 31 days, Alphadjo Cisse became the second-youngest Rossoneri player to reach this milestone in his first 10 appearances in the three-points-for-a-win era, after Alexandre Pato , who achieved it at 18 years and 189 days.

No team has scored more goals than Milan in the first 15 minutes of play in the five major European leagues right now underway (7, like Barcelona and Chelsea).

Milan are now unbeaten in all seven meetings against Frosinone in Serie A (W5 D2): among the teams against which they have never lost in the competition, the Rossoneri have played more games only against Pisa (14 – six also against Crotone and Lecco).

Milan have won five of their last six league games (L1), scoring at least two goals in each, after failing to win three of their previous four (D3). The last time they scored more than one goal in a run of Serie A matches was between September 2020 and January 2021, when they managed 15 games.

By Matt Law | 24 Nov 2026 12:49, Last updated: 24 Nov 2026 12:52.

Anderlecht will be aiming to make it three straight wins in the league stage of the Europa League when they travel to OFI Crete on Thursday night.

The visitors will bring a four-game unbeaten run in all competitions into this match, but Crete will enter the European fixture off the back of a 2-0 loss to Panathinaikos in the Greek Super League.

OFI have a record of two wins and two losses from their four matches in the league stage of this season's Europa League, with six points leaving them in 16th position in the overall table.

The Club started their league phase with a 2-0 win over Hoffenheim before losing back-to-back games in the competition against Rennes and Bayer Leverkusen.

Sources indicate that however, Christos Kontis' side posted a 2-0 victory over H. Beer Sheva in their last Europa League game on November 5, so they will be aiming to make it back-to-back wins in the tournament.

OFI are playing in the league stage/group stage of a major European tournament for the first time since the 1995-96 campaign, and this is also the first time that they have ever qualified for this round of the UEFA Cup/Europa League.

The Club have European matches to come against Benfica, Sturm Graz and Lech before the end of the group stage in early 2027.

Anderlecht, meanwhile, have also won two and lost two of their four matches in this season's Europa League league stage, with six points leaving them 15th in the table.

The Belgian club started their league phase with a 2-1 loss to Lyon, before going down 1-0 to Dinamo Zagreb in the middle of October, but they have won their last two matches in the tournament against Jagiellonia and Red Bull Salzburg to move onto six points.

Vitor Bruno's side will enter this match off the back of a 1-0 win over Leuven in the league, with the result leaving them in fifth position in Belgium's top flight.

Anderlecht will face Hoffenheim, Sunderland and Marseille in their three European matches after this one, and it would be a surprise if they were not present in the knockout round.

The Purple and Whites won this competition back in 1982-83, and this is their first Europa League league phase campaign since 2024-25.

OFI Crete form (all competitions):.

Anderlecht form (all competitions):.

Crete will be without the services of Kenan Kodro, Kresimir Krizmanic, Fotis Koutsoupias, Konstantinos Lagoudakis, Emmanouil Chnaris and Nikos Marinakis due to injury problems.

Taxiarchis Fountas has scored five times in 19 appearances this season, and the 31-year-old is set to feature in the final third of the field for the hosts.

Meanwhile, there should also be a position in the side for Thiago Nuss, who has provided seven goal contributions in all competitions for Crete this term.

As for Anderlecht, Ilay Camara and Lucas Hey are out of the match due to injury problems.

Mihajlo Cvetkovic has been in strong form for his Belgian club this season, scoring seven goals and registering two assists in 22 matches, and the 19-year-old will continue in the final third of the field.

There are also expected to be spots in the final third for Danylo Sikan and Jayden Onia-Seke.

OFI Crete possible starting lineup:.

Lilo; Shielis, Nikolaou, Poungouras; Dickmann, Bouchalakis, Androutsos, Athanasiou; Cantalapiedra, Nuss, Fountas.

Anderlecht possible starting lineup:.

Coosemans; Maamar, Omobamidele, Petrot, Augustinsson; Ambros, Llansana, Stroeykens, Onia-Seke; Sikan, Cvetkovic.

This is a difficult match to call; cases can be made for either side to pick up all three points, but we are expecting a close fixture to end with the points being shared.

#118133. ‘The worst COP ever’ offers a chance to learn from failure

📅 26 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 6m • 📚 Deep Dive (1215 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Nature ↗ Open Full Page

‘The worst COP ever’ offers a chance to learn from failure

📅 26 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1215 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nature

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, protesters on the final day of the COP31 climate conference in Antalya, Turkey.
  • Sources indicate that ‘The worst COP ever’ is how some people have described the United Nations COP31 climate meeting in Antalya, Turkey, which ended on 22 November.
  • The world’s first plastics treaty is in crisis: can it be salvaged?
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, protesters on the final day of the COP31 climate conference in Antalya, Turkey. Credit: Chris McGrath/Getty.

Sources indicate that ‘The worst COP ever’ is how some people have described the United Nations COP31 climate meeting in Antalya, Turkey, which ended on 22 November. COP31 was the first to take place after the confirmation that global warming will overshoot the safe limit of 1.5 °C above pre-industrial levels. Despite a two-day extension to the meeting and several proposals for an overarching political declaration or ‘cover decision’, delegates left after two weeks of talks without such an agreement.

The world’s first plastics treaty is in crisis: can it be salvaged?

The world’s first plastics treaty is in crisis: can it be salvaged?

In a recent development, drafted by the host nations (Turkey and Australia, this year), a cover decision is a statement that all countries can agree on at the end of the talks. It is not a legally binding text and is a relatively recent innovation. That participants failed to agree such a statement is not a surprise. It requires a willingness for give and take, which was in short supply because many of the countries that attended this year are at war, subject to economic and other sanctions, or involved in trade disputes. Furthermore, the United States, the world’s biggest economy and the largest historic carbon emitter, did not attend following its withdrawal from the COP process.

Delegates from the world’s poorest countries were angry that there was no mention of concrete measures to increase finance for climate adaptation — money that they will need to help them to become more resilient to climate shocks. Many delegates were also angry that the draft text did not include any reference to transitioning away from fossil fuels. Previous cover decisions have included such language, overcoming objections from fossil-fuel-producing states. This time, however, delegates from these states were more determined to block such wording.

It has been revealed that but there are key reasons why it would be wrong to conclude that such climate conferences have outlived their purpose — or that a consensus-based approach should be abandoned, as some have argued. There is always room to improve, but COP meetings are much more than what happens in the final days when high-level political representatives turn up.

Environmental treaties are paralysed — here’s how we can do better.

Environmental treaties are paralysed — here’s how we can do better.

First, these meetings mainly involve discussions between technical experts and observers — including many researchers — representing the countries that have signed up to the UN’s climate agreement, known as the UN Framework Convention on Climate Change. For most of the two weeks (and in many timetabled talks before a COP), delegates meet in working groups to discuss a spectrum of climate-change topics. The Antalya meeting discussions included how to accelerate electrification, cut methane emissions and mobilize latest finance to protect the world’s forests. Progress in these technical talks is often incremental. In contrast to the final days of a COP, which are organized around negotiations between political representatives, expert delegates focus on getting things done rather than posturing.

The second reason not to write off this COP is that it’s not uncommon for countries to leave meetings without a high-level agreement. Indeed, some previous ‘good’ outcomes needed earlier COP meetings to ‘fail’. The landmark COP21 Paris climate agreement signed in 2015, a legally binding text in which nations agreed to limit global warming to 1.5 °C, is perhaps the best-known example. In 2009, COP15 in Copenhagen resulted in deadlock. That failure prompted deeper thinking and discussions at subsequent COP meetings on the steps needed for the world to stay within safe climate limits, laying the groundwork for the Paris agreement.

According to recent reports, still, the current geopolitical climate is a substantial obstacle to progress, affecting not only COP climate meetings but also talks on other international agreements, such as a proposed treaty to end plastic pollution. Another set of talks occurring at the same time as COP31 — on setting international restrictions on autonomous weapons — also failed to reach an agreement and will resume in 2028.

In the case of both the climate and plastics talks, a relatively small group of countries — including Iran, Russia and Saudi Arabia, which are heavily reliant on fossil-fuel exports, among others — are blocking stronger action. Some researchers, as well as country delegates, say that the UN’s method of decision-making (that all countries must agree a consensus) is the problem, and question whether there should instead be a vote and a decision made by majority.

Trust and science: the essential elements missing from plastics treaty talks.

Trust and science: the essential elements missing from plastics treaty talks.

Recent findings suggest that there is some logic in changing the approach for the cover decisions to avoid the overtly self-interested blocking of action. But for many other decisions made at UN climate and other environment-related meetings, abandoning a consensus-based approach in favour of a vote would not be a good option.

In a recent development, the UN’s expert groups for example, including the scientists who are part of the Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change (which synthesizes studies to inform decisions), must continue to work through consensus. Delegates painstakingly review, debate and discuss evidence, before coming to a conclusion — and it is important that all those involved are brought in at this point.

A change to voting might, in some cases, mean faster results, but it would also undermine the principles that everyone owns the result and that global problems need global solutions.

In a recent development, it is right that, on reflecting on the COP in Antalya, many will ask what needs to change. And some aspects must. But altering how decisions are made should not be taken lightly. Climate change doesn’t respect borders. It won’t be solved by countries working on their own or in small groups.

📅 22 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (908 w)
📖 Baca

Mauricio Pochettino blames Man United's 'painful' thrashing at Liverpool on 'unfair' red card - after Roy Keane lashes out at Gary Neville for suggesting 4-0 defeat was an 'OK result' with 10 men

📅 22 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (908 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dailymail

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • By CHRIS WHEELER, NORTHERN SPORTS WRITER and LEWIS BROWNING, SPORTS REPORTER.
  • Published: 16:32 EST, 22 November 2026 | Updated: 10:28 EST, 24 November 2026.
  • Mauricio Pochettino suggested the Leny Yoro red card that had such an affect ontheir defeat by Liverpool game was 'unfair' and that their opponents should have been 'punished' too.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By CHRIS WHEELER, NORTHERN SPORTS WRITER and LEWIS BROWNING, SPORTS REPORTER.

Published: 16:32 EST, 22 November 2026 | Updated: 10:28 EST, 24 November 2026.

Mauricio Pochettino suggested the Leny Yoro red card that had such an affect ontheir defeat by Liverpool game was 'unfair' and that their opponents should have been 'punished' too.

Pochettino gave up his job as US national team coach to join United on Wednesday, but any hope of a upcoming manager 'bounce' evaporated after Yoro was sent off inside eight minutes and his team were thrashed 4-0.

It was the joint-heaviest defeat for a fresh United manager since Lal Hilditch a century ago, and leaves Pochettino's side second from bottom of the Premier League.

Recent findings suggest that 'So painful, so disappointed,' said the Argentine, who blamed the early red card for United's defeat. 'It's not OK to start a game in the Premier League with this situation. The game changed completely after eight minutes. Now we can explain everything, but the damage is done – it's so painful.

'It's clear that after eight minutes the proposal was in the bin. Do you think that is easy? Even the best team in the world playing in this situation concedes four goals or maybe more.

Industry observers note that 'We are not going to lose more than one game how we lost today. I take the responsibility, and we keep pushing.

Manchester United boss Mauricio Pochettino blamed Leny Yoro's red card for his side's defeat by Liverpool.

Yoro (right) was sent off for fouling Alexander Isak inside eight minutes of Sunday's game.

'We feel pain for this defeat, but we need to keep our heads up and translate that anger into energy to start to work from tomorrow for the next game.

'We are in a situation that this is very complicated. It's difficult, yes, but I think we fight, we made the effort, and I know how they feel now in the dressing-room.

According to recent reports, 'The players are feeling the pain of the result. I told them to be calm: it was an unfair situation that happened. We need to accept that reality. We need to try to increase our focus, concentration and make better decisions on the field.

'We also need to be critical on ourselves but some situations happened in the game that we are not happy.'.

Pochettino was unhappy that referee Sam Barrott indicated Yoro a straight red card for his challenge on Alexander Isak, having taken no action over a similar incident involving Jeremy Jacquet and Bryan Mbeumo in the Liverpool penalty box moments earlier.

Industry observers note that 'In Leny's case, it wasn't intentional. It was an unusual situation that is normal. Everyone who plays football can feel it,' added the United boss. 'If you review the VAR you can see for sure, he never had the intention to connect with Isak. The ball was going to the goalkeeper.

'If you look before, in the sixth minute, Jacquet on Mbeumo. If you compare the actions, that was a penalty. We were punished badly and they were not punished, that is the truth.'.

He later added: 'One centre-back made a mistake and wasn't punished and us, we made one mistake and we were punished.'.

Kobbie Mainoo and Bruno Fernandes agreed their team-mate should not have been sent off.

United midfielder Kobbie Mainoo agreed with Pochettino that it wasn't a red card.

In a recent development, 'No chance,' remarked Mainoo. 'The ball is already with the keeper, and they're both running full speed. What can he do?

'I feel like the game has been taken out of our hands early by a red card that I don't think can be a red card.

'It's hard but no-one is going to save us. We have to come together and keep digging, keep fighting, and it will come round.'.

Captain Bruno Fernandes, meanwhile, added: 'I can understand the fall, but it's never a red card, and I think it's too many referees on the pitch and too many on VAR with a long time to see, do it in slow motion, and make a mistake like this which can change the game.'.

Gary Neville, who was left slapping himself in the face in shock live on Sky Sports, was pleased with damage control on, with United conceding four when it looked at one point that it would have been many more.

Former United captain Roy Keane, however, wasn't, and took aim at his ex-side's display.

'I thought United were desperate,' he said. 'So bad. Neville's OK with 4-0? Are you telling me they could have done better? 4-0 is not too bad with 10 men? Has anyone ever got a result with 10 men? It can be done.

Roy Keane (pictured), meanwhile, questioned why Gary Neville was pleased with the scoreline.

'People who played for the club noted 4-0 is not too bad? Wow. Fans are applauding. Applauding what? Performing rubbish?

'Liverpool were excellent but how easy did United make it for them? This team two years ago finished 15th. The last year or two, we're talking. We're blaming the board, blaming ownership, blaming managers. When do the players take responsibility for some decision-making?

Sources indicate that 'Liverpool probably should have scored eight, probably eight or nine, unbelievable chances they had. And everyone's coming off the pitch saying four is not too bad? I feel like swearing.'.

“Annoyed” Kevin De Bruyne faces uncertain Napoli future ahead of Man City return

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (786 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Oliver Thomas | 24 Nov 2026 13:05.
  • Manchester City legend Kevin De Bruyne is preparing for an emotional homecoming at the Etihad Stadium on Tuesday night, though his current spell with Napoli has been clouded by transfer speculation and internal friction.
  • After winning 19 trophies during a glittering 10-year career at Man City, the 35-year-old playmaker reluctantly left the club at the end of the 2024-25 season when the decision was made to not extend his contract.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Oliver Thomas | 24 Nov 2026 13:05.

Manchester City legend Kevin De Bruyne is preparing for an emotional homecoming at the Etihad Stadium on Tuesday night, though his current spell with Napoli has been clouded by transfer speculation and internal friction.

After winning 19 trophies during a glittering 10-year career at Man City, the 35-year-old playmaker reluctantly left the club at the end of the 2024-25 season when the decision was made to not extend his contract.

De Bruyne subsequently signed for Napoli as a free agent, embarking on a fresh challenge in Italian football, but his debut campaign was struck by injury, starting only 16 matches across all competitions as Napoli surrendered their Serie A crown to Inter Milan.

The Belgium international has since played in all 16 games for Napoli across Serie A and the Champions League this term, chipping in with four goals and two assists while operating in a deeper midfield position under head coach Massimiliano Allegri.

De Bruyne is part of an aging Napoli side that are currently languishing down in eighth place in Serie A and sit 27th in the Champions League standings after losing three of their opening four League Phase games.

Tensions boiled over during Napoli’s heavy 4-1 UCL loss at Porto earlier this month, where teammates had to separate De Bruyne and striker Lorenzo Lucca following an angry on-pitch row.

"Speaking about the pitch, De Bruyne is the best player this year at Napoli. The point is that the whole team is having difficulties, Naples-based journalist Vincenzo Credendino told BBC Sport.

In a recent development, "We saw that there is a problem, at least between De Bruyne and Lorenzo Lucca. Their acting was very, very clear and I think that in that time, the two of them were wrong.

"On one hand you cannot swear at another team-mate but on the other hand, De Bruyne reproached Lucca without encouraging him, so it was a bad show.".

As De Bruyne enters the twilight years of his career, it has been suggested that the “spark never really ignited” between the midfielder and the Naples outfit, raising uncertainty over his future at the club.

Recent findings suggest that when asked about his future at a press conference ahead of Napoli’s Champions League clash with Man City, De Bruyne mentioned: "Not a lot I can say for the moment. I have played at 100% until now and obviously I am not 20 years old, I am turning 36.

"There is a lot of things going in my mind but there is not a lot to say. I am playing good football, trying to help the team to do well and it has been a bit of a challenging season with a lot of things happening.".

De Bruyne will soon be entering the final six months of his Napoli contract and will be free to negotiate pre-contract agreements with foreign clubs in January.

De Bruyne has also expressed his annoyance over the backlash he and his family have received following controversial comments made by the player’s wife in September.

His wife Michele reportedly told Belgian magazine NINA about their desire to move back to Belgium, saying "the sooner we get there, the better" as De Bruyne leads a "very restricted life" in Naples.

Addressing the media fallout, De Bruyne replied: "To be honest, I am pretty annoyed because if you read the article, that none of you have read, to understand what she said.

"I was away in Belgium and a lot of noise came and a lot of bad reactions to my wife and family. I saw pictures of my house, I don't think it is OK but it is what it is and some press created this in Italy. I don't know why.

According to recent reports, "Nobody knows my life, you will never know. People who work with me are not allowed to say anything but obviously it is something that I take away and think about. It has not been nice for my wife or for my family.".

De Bruyne has since been linked with a sensational Premier League return in January, while Dutch giants PSV Eindhoven are understood to have failed with a €2m (£1.7m) opening offer to sign him in the Latest Year, with Napoli valuing the midfielder closer to €8m (£6.7m), according to Credendino.

Napoli boss Allegri has interestingly refused to rule out a mid-season departure for De Bruyne, stating on Monday that transfer decisions are "down to the players and who wants to leave" once January arrives.

Meanwhile, De Bruyne has spoken out for the first time since Man City were found guilty of breaching Premier League financial regulations.
